verdict.rationale: Isaac documents ROS 2 integration for validating robot stacks in simulation, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing, and portable Isaac Lab policy bundles for real hardware, so the same stack can plausibly target both sim and robot. However, no source explicitly says identical code runs unchanged on both. The community report of sim-to-real drift concerns physics fidelity, not code portability, so it does not contradict this story. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement or guide showing the same code switching between sim and real hardware without changes, and independent hands-on corroboration of a no-rewrite sim-to-real workflow.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can run the same robot code against simulation and the real robot without a rewrite
